relevance_note: The paper gives individual-level clinical, neuropathological and post-mortem data for one identifiable patient with SSADHD ("a 37 y.o. male patient with succinic semialdehyde dehydrogenase deficiency (SSADHD)").
method_note: Single case report (post-mortem study, part II of a series). I read the whole Markdown file (body text, all tables 1a-8 and figure legends); no table was transcribed by script, so all quotes were copied by hand from the file. Only one in-scope person is described: the paper's own adult male patient (labelled 'patient', rule 5; no label such as P1 is used). 'The family of the patient' is mentioned only as consenting/acknowledged, with no individual-level detail, so no relative row was created. The patient was first reported by Haan et al (1985) and again by Kirby et al (2020), so publications.cites_prior_report_of_same_patients = true. Judgment calls: (1) the paper never prints an ALDH5A1 variant description for this patient (no cDNA/protein string anywhere in the text, tables, figures or references); I kept one variants row with variant_original_string = 'not reported' under the v3 rule for a person tied to ALDH5A1 but with no printed description - the row should be excluded from variant counts. (2) 'global developmental delays' is the only statement of cognitive/developmental impairment; I mapped it to the checklist item 'intellectual disability' (observed) but did not extend it to 'gross or fine motor deficits' (not reported), and I flag this mapping as uncertain. (3) Age at diagnosis is not stated (the general sentence 'most patients are diagnosed in early childhood' is not about this person) and the basis of the diagnosis is not described ('Because his diagnosis was known'), so both are 'not reported'. (4) EEG/MRI/CT were explicitly not undertaken, so the EEG and MRI checklist items are 'not reported', not 'excluded'. (5) Tissue-level statements ('Samples of the peripheral nervous system, striatal muscle, spinal cord, and peripheral nerves were not obtained at autopsy') describe missing samples, not absent clinical features, and were not recorded as excluded. (6) Lipid mass/molar composition and gene-expression values are biochemical results about the same single patient; I did not create phenotypic_features rows for them. No internal contradictions about this person's features were found (the cortical lipid increase is discussed as contradicting prior mouse studies, not as an internal contradiction).
